title: perf-bench-scratch-dylan-cho-2026-03-30
content:
Scratchpad: perf runs + quick takeaways
Owner: Dylan Cho
Date: 2026-03-30 (runs 03-30 09:00-12:00 UTC)
Context: trying to reproduce recent degradation in p95 for small batches after KV-cache change (INF-4123). Baseline = llm-open-3b-8q (8-bit quant) on A100-80GB (p4d), runtime v2.4.1-rc.

Environment:
- Model: llm-open-3b-8q (8-bit seq-opt)
- Runtime: serving-runtime v2.4.1-rc (hash: abcdef)
- HW: A100-80GB (p4d), single GPU
- OS/container: org/base-runtime:2026-02-15
- Inference flags: kv_cache_enabled=true (default), continuous_batching=true, batcher.max_batch=32
- Load generator: locust-based harness (github PR linked)

Test matrix (short):
- Sequence length: 32 tokens output (prompt ~16 tokens)
- Batch sizes: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32
- Concurrency (workers): 1, 2, 4
- Reps: 5 runs each, report median across reps

Key results (median across reps):
Batch=1, conc=1 -> p50=88ms, p95=210ms, qps=11.3
Batch=2, conc=1 -> p50=95ms, p95=230ms, qps=20.5
Batch=4, conc=1 -> p50=130ms, p95=310ms, qps=30.8
Batch=8, conc=1 -> p50=200ms, p95=520ms, qps=38.4
Batch=16, conc=1 -> p50=360ms, p95=980ms, qps=44.6
Batch=32, conc=1 -> p50=820ms, p95=2.1s, qps=49.2

Notes:
- Absolute p50 numbers are in-line with previous baseline for batch>=4. The regression is most obvious at batch=1 where p95 increased ~2x vs run on v2.3.8.
- Increasing concurrency from 1->4 increases qps linearly for small batches but p95 gets worse when conc>2 for batch<=2. Likely contention on dispatcher locks or cache lock.

Quick ASCII throughput chart (qps vs batch at conc=1):
batch: 1   2   4    8    16   32
 qps : 11  20  31   38   45   49
(Throughput scaling diminishing after 16, expected due to token-level compute dominates memory-bound work)

Micro-observations (logs / traces):
- Tracing shows an extra 40-70ms in request queue time for batch=1 on v2.4.1-rc (not present on v2.3.8).
- KV-cache hit path unchanged, but lock acquisition time increased (stack: batcher->req-queue->kv-cache->lock).
- GPU utilization steady ~92% for large batches; for batch=1 GPU idle spikes during short polls (inefficient wakeups).

Hypothesis:
1) New queue refactor (PR in INF-4123) introduced a contention point when requests arrive very sparse (single-item batches). Lock held while performing small synchronous ops before enqueueing to worker threads.
2) Wakeup latency for worker pool increased due to condition variable unusual scheduling on this kernel/container combo.

Quick experiments to validate (done during run):
- Disabled kv_cache (kv_cache_enabled=false): p95 for batch=1 dropped from 210ms->120ms. Suggests part of the added latency is inside cache path, possibly lock ordering.
- Set batcher.max_batch=8 (instead of 32): p95 for batch=1 unchanged but overall qps slight drop for large flows.
- Short-circuit enqueue: local patch that moves minimal small-op outside lock reduced p95 to ~130ms for batch=1.

Conclusions / next steps:
- Root cause likely lock+enqueue path introduced in INF-4123. Quick mitigation: revert the refactor or apply minimal patch to avoid holding the lock across cache lookup.
- Longer term: add a fast-path for single-item requests (bypass batching queue), and add metrics for lock hold time and queue wait distribution.
- Add unit + stress tests that simulate sparse arrivals to prevent regressions.

TODOs (action items):
- [ ] Open PR with minimal lock-scope fix (branch: fix/shorten-enqueue-lock) — I started local patch, need review (assign to Sam).
- [ ] Add queue wait histograms to runtime metrics (SLO alert if p95 queue_wait > 100ms) — Jira INF-4181.
- [ ] Re-run tests on H100 instance (we only tested A100 today) to see if wakeup behavior differs.
- [ ] Coordinate with SRE to reproduce in Dedicated env (customer impact probable).

Links / references:
- INF ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4123
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/567

Notes-to-self:
- Keep raw logs for 03-30-09:00 run (saved to s3://redwood-perf/dylan/2026-03-30/)
- Follow up with Maya on adding unit test harness for sparse arrival scenarios.
- Capture kernel/oom/syscalls if repro in Dedicated to rule out host-level preemption.

End of scratchpad.
